summary: Nirmal Chandra Sinha (1911–1997) was a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology who studied at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta. He served as founder director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology (1958–1987) and Centenary Professor at the University of Calcutta (1971).
Nirupam Chakma is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Tilak Kariyawasam and Fa Qing (attested 2015).
Noa Gal is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies who earned a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under the supervision of Richard Gombrich (attested 2003).

Noa Ronkin is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. She completed a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford (Wolfson College) under Richard Gombrich, studied under Shlomo Biderman, and served as Lecturer and Research Fellow at Stanford University (attested 2005).

Noboru Karashima (1933–2015) was a historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held positions at the University of Tokyo (1964–1994, concluding as Professor Emeritus) and served as a professor at Taisho University (~1994–2008).

Noboru Miyata (1936–2000) was a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and folklore history. He studied at Tokyo University of Education and the University of Tsukuba, later serving as Professor of Folklore at Tsukuba (~1978–1997) and at Kanagawa University (~1997–2000).
Noboru Ueda is a scholar in Buddhist studies and other fields who held posts at the University of Tokyo (attested 1990) and as a professor at Mejiro University (attested 2015).

Nobuchiyo Kotani (1944–) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Otani University and Kyoto University under Yuichi Kajiyama, Noritoshi Aramaki, Hajime Sakurabe, and Ichijo Ogawa, later serving as professor at Otani University (~1987–2014).

Nobuhiko Kobayashi is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied at Kyoto University and under Yutaka Ochihara. He has held positions at the University of Toronto (attested 1969), Kyoto University (attested 1979), and Taisho University (attested 2026).

Nobuhiro Ota (1969–) is an Indologist and historian who completed undergraduate and graduate studies at the University of Tokyo. He has held academic posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, becoming an associate professor in 2007 and professor in 2021.
Nobukatsu Komai is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied as a research student at Taisho University and served as a full-time researcher at Chisan Denpōin (attested 2014).
Nobumasa Hibi (1932–) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Rissho University (completing studies in 1959) and later served there as an assistant professor (attested 1972).

Tensho Miyazaki (1978–) is a scholar of Buddhist, Indological, and Iranian/Central Asian studies who earned a doctorate at the University of Tokyo (~2006–2011). He held research posts at Toyo University (~2011–2014) and the University of Tokyo (~2014).

Nobumi Iyanaga (1948–) is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1968–1969). He held a research contract at the EFEO Tokyo Centre (2008–2014) and lectured at the University of Tokyo (attested 2003).
Nobuo Otsuka (1957–) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed doctoral studies at Taisho University (~1982–1987) and later served there as a researcher (attested 1995).

Nobuyoshi Yamabe (1960–) is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. at Yale under Stanley Weinstein, also studying at Osaka and Otani universities. He has served as a professor at Tokyo University of Agriculture (2003) and Waseda University (2015).

Nobuyuki Kaji (1936–) is a scholar of philosophy and Sinology who studied at Kyoto University and Tohoku University. He held academic posts including professor at Osaka University (1984–1998) and specially invited professor at Ritsumeikan University (2008–2015).

Nobuyuki Watase (1941–) is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who earned a master's degree at Kyoto University (~1964–1966). He served as an assistant professor at Tokai University (~1985–2007) and as president of Kobe Shukugawa Gakuin University (~2007–2010).

Nobuyuki Yamagiwa (1952–) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a lecturing post at Bukkyo University (attested 1997–2002) and a professorship at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).

Nobuyuki Yoshimoto (1940–) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University under Issai Funahashi and Genjun Sasaki. He held multiple academic and research positions at Otani University between ~1972 and ~2006.
